Inspiring Excellence
Welcome to Tooting Primary School
At Tooting Primary we aim to produce leaders of the future by igniting a love of learning in our pupils from an early age. Our pupils benefit from an array of experiences within and beyond the school gates.
We are proud of the opportunities we offer - learning to play musical instruments, food technology in our purpose- built space and taking full advantage of the close transport links for excursions further afield.
We are a strong community, providing quality education for pupils before, during and after school through lessons as well as extra -curricular activities.
We have a committed parent and governing body who share our passion for the school and its endeavours. Through high expectations of our pupils and our staff, we strive to live up to our school motto and inspire excellence!
You are warmly invited to come and see for yourself.
Jacqueline Wilson Headteacher

Vision & Values
Our vision and values shape everything we do, helping children grow into confident, responsible and successful learners.
We aim to create a safe, supportive learning environment and a welcoming community where everyone feels valued, respected and able to thrive. Through high expectations, strong relationships and a love of learning, we encourage every child to achieve their full potential.
Our Vision
Every child is successful, inspired to achieve excellence and able to enjoy the journey towards reaching their full potential.
How We Achieve This
1. High Expectations
We set ambitious academic and personal goals for every child, inspiring them to strive for excellence while providing the support they need to succeed.
We encourage curiosity, creativity and enjoyment in learning, helping children develop a lifelong passion for knowledge and personal growth.
3. Global Citizenship
We help children understand the wider world, value diversity and develop a strong sense of responsibility towards others and the environment.
4. Lifelong Learners
We equip children with the skills, resilience and adaptability needed to thrive in an ever-changing world.
5. Values and Nurturing
We create a caring environment where kindness, resilience, responsibility and respect are taught, modelled and celebrated every day.
Preparing children for life beyond primary school
Our values underpin our aspirations for every child. We want children to be confident, resilient and compassionate individuals who embrace challenges, learn from setbacks and believe in their ability to achieve great things.
Our School Values
We treat everyone with respect. We value what each member of our community adds to the success of our school.
We take responsibility for our actions. We try to correct any mistakes that we make.
We are consistent. We recognise that achieving good outcomes can be challenging. We keep trying.
We consider others. We work together as a team. We help where we can.

Music
Music is an important part of school life, with opportunities for all children to explore instruments and develop an appreciation of the enjoyment music can bring.
Across the school, pupils learn to play a range of percussion instruments and take part in regular singing sessions.
In Lower Key Stage 2 (Years 3 and 4), children receive weekly strings tuition, learning either the violin or mini-cello. In Upper Key Stage 2 (Years 5 and 6), they can continue with their chosen instrument and have the opportunity to join the school orchestra.
Additional Music Lessons
Instrumental lessons are available through Wandsworth Music, the borough’s specialist music service, which provides high-quality tuition in schools.
Lessons are typically 30 minutes long and can be taken individually or in small groups, with a range of instruments available. Teaching takes place during the school day.

Wraparound Care
Activ Camps provides our Breakfast Club and After School Club, offering safe, engaging childcare before and after the school day.
With more than 20 years' experience delivering childcare and activity programmes across South London, Activ Camps offers a welcoming environment where children can play, socialise, relax and enjoy a wide range of activities led by experienced staff.
Flexible booking options are available. Parents and carers can book regular sessions throughout the week or individual days to suit their family's needs.
Our Clubs
7:45am – Start of School
Children are welcomed each morning and offered a healthy breakfast, including a hot option each day.
Sessions finish with a fun group activity to help children start the day positively and ready to learn.
10% discount available for full-week bookings.
End of School – 5:55pm
Children enjoy a variety of activities including sports, games, crafts and creative projects in a safe and inclusive environment.
Healthy snacks and light meals are provided during each session.
10% discount available for full-week bookings.
Breakfast Club + After School Club
For families requiring childcare before and after school, combined wraparound care offers the best value.
Save £2.00 per day and up to £20.50 per week when booking full weeks.
Activities
Children take part in a wide variety of age-appropriate activities throughout the week, including:
All sessions are supervised by fully trained staff. Activ Camps operates with staff-to-child ratios of approximately 1:10, ensuring children receive excellent care and support.
Team games and sports

Parachute games
Arts and crafts
Creative projects
Indoor and outdoor play
Group challenges and themed activities
Booking
Places are popular and we recommend booking early, particularly for regular sessions.

Starting School
Starting school is an exciting milestone for children and families, and we are committed to making the transition as smooth, positive and enjoyable as possible.
We know that beginning school can bring a mixture of excitement, anticipation and sometimes a few worries too. Our experienced Early Years team works closely with families to help every child feel happy, confident and ready for their first day.
Starting school in September? Our Reception Open Days run from 23 September to 2 December.
Your Starting School Journey
1. School Place Offered
You receive your Reception place offer and welcome information from the school.
2. Welcome Information
We share key information about starting school, routines, expectations and important dates.
3. Transition Visits
Your child visits school, meets staff and begins to explore their new learning environment.
Families have opportunities to meet staff, ask questions and share information about their child.
5. Ready for September
Children begin school feeling confident, familiar with routines and excited about learning.
Getting to Know Your Child
Before children join us, we take time to learn about their interests, strengths and individual needs. This helps us create a positive start to school life and ensures that every child feels welcomed and valued from day one.
Transition visits and meetings with families help us understand:
Every child is unique. We use what we learn during transition to plan personalised support and help children settle quickly into school life.

Working Together
A strong partnership between home and school is one of the most important factors in helping children thrive. We encourage regular communication and provide many opportunities for families to become involved in school life.
Have a question? Please get in touch with the school office. We are always happy to help and support families preparing for their child's first year at school.

Music
Music is an important part of school life, with opportunities for all children to explore instruments and develop an appreciation of the enjoyment music can bring.
Across the school, pupils learn to play a range of percussion instruments and take part in regular singing sessions.
In Lower Key Stage 2 (Years 3 and 4), children receive weekly strings tuition, learning either the violin or mini-cello. In Upper Key Stage 2 (Years 5 and 6), they can continue with their chosen instrument and have the opportunity to join the school orchestra.
Additional Music Lessons
Instrumental lessons are available through Wandsworth Music, the borough’s specialist music service, which provides high-quality tuition in schools.
Lessons are typically 30 minutes long and can be taken individually or in small groups, with a range of instruments available. Teaching takes place during the school day.
